summary: Brunei waives visas in tiers — 90 days for US, Canadian and European passports, 30 days for several Asian, Gulf and European nationalities, and 14 days for most ASEAN neighbors — while Australians and four Gulf nationalities obtain a visa on arrival and most other travelers apply in advance for a visit visa through a Bruneian mission.

primarySources.name: Immigration and National Registration Department, Brunei Darussalam

declarations.name: Brunei E-Arrival Card
declarations.text: Foreign visitors must submit the E-Arrival Card online before travelling to Brunei — it may be requested at check-in. Register on the Immigration Department's portal imm.gov.bn, then create the card under 'Travel Cards'. You do not need one if you are not passing through immigration.

currencyLimits.text: The US Department of State gives BND 15,000 (about US$11,000) as Brunei's currency restriction, both on entry and on exit. No Brunei government source we could read states the threshold.

notes: The UK says the sale of alcohol and tobacco is illegal in Brunei. Non-Muslims aged 17 and over may bring in a limited amount of alcohol, which must be declared to customs on arrival and drunk in private.

The UK says drug offences can carry the death penalty in Brunei. Canada lists possessing pornographic material, firearms or weapons, gambling, and promoting any religion other than Islam among activities that are illegal and severely punished.

payments.text: No official source we could read describes how widely cards are accepted in Brunei. The UK notes that foreign-registered cars can buy fuel only at designated filling stations, where you can usually pay only in cash.

safety.text: Brunei has very low crime and is among the safest countries in Southeast Asia. The main considerations are legal and cultural: strict rules on alcohol, drugs and public behavior apply to visitors as well as residents.

bestTimeToVisit.text: Canada's travel advice gives Brunei's rainy (monsoon) seasons as September to January and May to July, so February to April and August fall between them. The CIA World Factbook describes the climate as tropical: hot, humid and rainy.

idp.text: Brunei is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

tips.text: The UK says the sale of alcohol is illegal in Brunei. Non-Muslims aged 17 and over may bring in a limited amount for private consumption, and it must be declared to customs on arrival.

The UK says Brunei's penalties for drug offences are severe and in some cases include the death penalty; Canada says death is the mandatory penalty for many narcotics offences, including trafficking even very small amounts. Never carry anything across the border for someone else.
The UK says that during Ramadan it is against the law to be seen eating or drinking in public during fasting hours, and that you must not smoke in public.
The UK advises dressing modestly in Brunei, for example not wearing shorts in government and public buildings such as health centres.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Brunei?
faq.answer: Many visitors do not. US, Canadian and EU passport holders get 90 days visa-free, the UK 90 days, several Asian, Gulf and European nationalities get 30 days, and most ASEAN neighbors get 14 days. Australians and four Gulf nationalities obtain a visa on arrival, and remaining nationalities apply in advance for a visit visa through a Bruneian mission — no official Brunei source describes an online e-Visa.

faq.question: Do Australians need a visa for Brunei?
faq.answer: Australians obtain a visa on arrival, single or multiple entry, for stays up to 30 days. Bring the fee in cash: BND 20 for single entry, BND 30 for multiple entry.

faq.question: Can I drink alcohol in Brunei?
faq.answer: Alcohol cannot be bought in Brunei: the UK says its sale is illegal. Non-Muslims aged 17 and over may bring in a limited amount, which must be declared to customs on arrival and drunk in private.

faq.question: What is the Brunei E-Arrival Card?
faq.answer: A digital arrival declaration that foreign visitors must submit online before travelling to Brunei: the UK government says it may be requested at check-in, and that you do not need one if you are not passing through immigration. Register on the Immigration Department's portal, imm.gov.bn, then create the card under 'Travel Cards'.

faq.question: How long can US citizens stay in Brunei?
faq.answer: US passport holders can enter visa-free for up to 90 days — the most generous tier of Brunei's waiver scheme, shared with Canadian, EU and UK passports.
